basic_identification.full_title: Medical Textiles — Bedsheet and Pillow Cover — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Textiles / Technical Textiles for Medtech Applications (approved by the Textile Division Council and finalized by the Technical Textiles for Medtech Applications Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Technical Textiles for Medtech Applications Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, construction, material, dimensions, tolerances, performance testing, and packaging schedules for disposable (single-use) and reusable (multiple-use) bedsheets and pillow covers intended for medical and clinical purposes in hospitals, clinics, and other healthcare environments to aid in infection control, hygiene, and patient comfort.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Medical Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all medical bedsheets and pillow covers (disposable or reusable) manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 17630:2021 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified hospital bedding is a criminal offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. MSMEs are granted phased transition timelines, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to healthcare bedsheets and pillow covers.

requirements.detail: Every commercial pack of bedsheets and pillow covers conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to certify compliance.
Bedsheets and pillow covers must be manufactured from spunlace and/or spunbond non-woven fabric, or woven fabric; made of cotton, polyester, or their blends.
Products are classified as: a) Single Use (Disposable); b) Reusable. If reusable, the manufacturer must declare the maximum wash cycles / life cycle of the product.

The manufacture and preparation of the bedsheets and pillow covers must be conducted under proper hygienic conditions. The manufacturer must implement and record a systematic factory hygiene maintenance program.
The finished products must be clean and free from lumping, holes, tears, or chemicals/substances that can cause tendering or degradation during storage.

To prevent tearing or splitting during patient handling, the fabric must satisfy strict minimum mechanical limits on: a) Tensile strength (dry and wet) tested per IS 15891 (Part 3) or IS 1969 (Part 1); b) Bursting strength (dry and wet) tested per IS 1966 (Part 1); c) Seam strength (dry and wet) to verify stitch robustness.

Fabric dyes must show high stability against clinical exposure, satisfying specified limits on: colorfastness to rubbing (dry and wet), colorfastness to perspiration (acidic and alkaline), colorfastness to light, and colorfastness to washing.
The pH of the cold aqueous extract of the material must be strictly verified as skin-friendly when tested in accordance with IS 1390.

To maintain hygiene in sterile environments, the total viable microbial count (bacterial and fungal bioburden) must satisfy strict limits when tested as per the dilution and plating out methods of ISO 11737-1.
The fabric must show low linting and low particle release properties under standard dynamic testing to prevent aerosol contamination of sterile clinical spaces.

requirements.requirement_type: Amended Biocompatibility Evaluation (Table 2 - Sl No. viii)
requirements.detail: Under Amendment No. 2, the biocompatibility evaluation is optional. If specified by the purchaser, the raw material must pass in-vitro cytotoxicity testing per IS/ISO 10993 (Part 5) with a result of 'non-cytotoxic', and pass irritation and skin sensitization tests.
The fabric must limit water-soluble chemicals to prevent leaching or chemical contact with patients.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 17630 : 2021 is the mandatory national Indian Standard safety specification regulating single-use (disposable) and reusable medical bedsheets and pillow covers used in hospitals, clinics, and other healthcare facilities. Formulated under India's statutory Medical Textiles Quality Control Order (QCO), all clinical bedsheets and pillow covers sold or imported in India must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to ensure infection control, hygiene, and patient safety. It specifies material varieties (woven cotton/polyester blends, or spunlace/spunbond non-woven fabrics) and mandates strict limits on mechanical strength (tensile, bursting, and seam strength), skin-compatibility (pH and water-soluble substances), dye stability (colorfastness), and microbial cleanliness. Amendment No. 2 (June 2024) refines the standard by making biocompatibility testing optional but enforcing strict 'non-cytotoxic' verification if conducted, and mandating that the package be printed with the word 'MEDICAL USE' and biocompatibility details.
